title: Build a Bounded TTL-Aware LRU Cache

company_style_tags.relevance_rationale: Exercises general coding correctness, data-structure selection, and edge-case communication rather than claiming interview provenance.
Practices implementation fluency and complexity reasoning relevant to large product engineering environments.

learning_objectives: Combine a hash map and recency ordering to meet cache bounds.
Make expiration behavior deterministic through clock injection.
Explain correctness, complexity, and production concurrency trade-offs.
problem_statement: Implement `BoundedTTLCache`, an in-memory cache with a fixed positive capacity and per-entry time-to-live. `get(key)` returns an unexpired value and makes the key most recently used. It raises `KeyError` for missing or expired keys and removes an expired key before raising. `set(key, value, ttl_seconds)` rejects non-positive TTLs, overwrites an existing key, removes expired entries, and evicts the least recently used live entry until the cache is within capacity. The constructor receives a zero-argument monotonic clock so tests do not depend on wall time. `len(cache)` returns the number of live entries.
candidate_instructions: Use only the Python standard library.
Do not read the wall clock directly; use the injected clock.
State the worst-case time and space complexity of every public operation.
Discuss, but do not implement, a thread-safe production variant.
interviewer_instructions: Reveal overwrite semantics only if the candidate asks.
Ask how the implementation behaves when every entry expires simultaneously.
Do not reveal the OrderedDict reference approach before the candidate commits to a design.
constraints: ttl_seconds must be greater than zero
Keys are hashable and values may be any Python object
The clock is monotonic and returns seconds as a float
assumptions: A single cache instance is used by one thread for the base exercise.
Expiration occurs when clock() is greater than or equal to expires_at.
Refreshing recency on get is required; set also makes the key most recent.
expected_clarifying_questions: Does get refresh the TTL or only recency?
Is an item expired at exactly its expiration timestamp?
What should happen when set overwrites an existing key?
Must expired entries count toward capacity or length?

hints.text: Separate O(1) lookup from recency ordering.
The standard library has an ordered mapping with move-to-end behavior.
Store an absolute expiration time and compare with >=, not >.

common_mistakes: Using wall-clock time, which can move backward.
Counting expired entries in len or capacity decisions.
Forgetting to update recency when overwriting or reading.
Treating an entry as live at exactly expires_at.
Claiming all set operations are O(1) while scanning for expired entries.
strong_answer_indicators: Defines expiration boundary semantics before coding.
Keeps lookup and recency changes localized and testable.
Reports the O(capacity) worst-case purge honestly.
Explains lock granularity and loader stampede concerns for production.
weak_answer_indicators: Evicts a live key while expired keys remain.
Silently accepts a zero or negative TTL.
Adds a global lock without discussing contention or callback boundaries.
follow_up_questions: How would you prevent duplicate concurrent loads for the same key?
How would you make expiration cleanup sublinear without unbounded stale heap entries?
What metrics would distinguish a capacity problem from a TTL-selection problem?
harder_variants: Add an async get_or_load operation with per-key request coalescing and cancellation-safe cleanup.
Support weighted capacity while preserving deterministic eviction and metrics.
easier_variants: Remove TTL and implement a capacity-only LRU cache.
Provide get and set but omit len and overwrite-specific tests.

mode_specification.input_specification: Construct with `(capacity, clock)`, then call `set`, `get`, and `len` directly.
mode_specification.output_specification: Methods return stored values or None as documented and raise ValueError/KeyError for invalid or unavailable data.
